con-source-dependence-and-johannine-dist.words: Mark probably preceded and supplied Matthew and Luke, whereas John diverges substantially from those Synoptic accounts in miracles, encounters, teachings, and extended speeches.
con-source-dependence-and-johannine-dist.critique: Strongest feature: The argument clearly distinguishes probable Synoptic dependence from Johannine distinctiveness, illustrates the latter with concrete categories of material, and directly explains why four documents cannot automatically be counted as four independent witnesses. Principal limitation: The cited comparison establishes substantial literary difference more securely than it establishes the precise direction, causes, or historical consequences of every relationship, while the move does not engage a developed continuity interpretation. Live burden: The skeptical case still must show how dependence and distinctiveness affect particular resurrection traditions, rather than allowing broad source relationships alone to determine the reliability of every narrated event. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise probabilistic wording, coherent source-critical relevance, and substantial textual warrant, tempered by limited engagement with competing explanations of the same documentary pattern.

con-calibrated-existence-baseline.words: Paul’s reported meeting with James strongly supports Jesus’s existence, yet that early evidence alone does not establish the content of Jesus’s deeds or sayings.
con-calibrated-existence-baseline.critique: Strongest feature: The move uses a specific early datum, Paul’s contact with James, to support Jesus’s existence while immediately and expressly limiting what that evidence can establish about particular sayings, deeds, or narratives. Principal limitation: The argument does not compare alternative interpretations of the kinship designation, and its carefully bounded baseline contributes less directly to the central dispute about Gospel reliability and resurrection than the larger source-critical arguments do. Live burden: The skeptical route must connect this commendable calibration to principled criteria for deciding which additional claims survive scrutiny, rather than merely contrasting a secure minimum with everything more controversial. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional coherence, explicit qualification, and concrete evidentiary grounding, moderated by subsidiary relevance and the absence of sustained engagement with an opposing interpretation of James’s relationship.

con-anonymous-late-changing-transmission.words: The Gospels retain credible history but resist straightforward reading because anonymous, later non-eyewitness authors transmitted changing oral stories in another language and produced contradictions.
con-anonymous-late-changing-transmission.critique: Strongest feature: The move assembles anonymity, third-person narration, linguistic distance, later composition, oral transmission, and contradiction into a coherent reason for bounded rather than wholesale confidence, while expressly preserving the possibility of credible history. Principal limitation: The transition from conditions permitting change to demonstrated alteration remains compressed, because the argument provides limited evidence about how frequently, directionally, or materially the relevant traditions changed before composition. Live burden: The skeptical case must identify which resurrection claims are weakened by dependence or transmission and explain why preserved local knowledge or mediated eyewitness material cannot adequately support those particular claims. Locked score: The very strong band reflects broad central-burden contact, stable qualifications, fair acknowledgment of possible preservation, and a strong documentary foundation, with restraint for the underdeveloped bridge between transmission risk and actual corruption.

pro-miracle-content-method-challenge.words: When two stories share the same transmission history but only one contains a miracle, historians must explain whether miraculous content itself warrants additional distrust.
pro-miracle-content-method-challenge.critique: Strongest feature: The controlled hypothetical isolates miraculous content while holding lateness, oral transmission, and linguistic change constant, thereby forcing the skeptical historian to articulate whether rarity, rather than source defects alone, changes the evidentiary assessment. Principal limitation: As a diagnostic question, it supplies neither empirical base rates nor an actual comparison showing that the resurrection evidence matches an ordinary report in independence, quality, and transmission history. Live burden: The pro route must move from exposing a possible methodological asymmetry to demonstrating how real resurrection testimony overcomes concrete alternatives such as dependence, witness error, embellishment, or invention. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional clarity, logical focus, direct contact with the governing historical-method burden, and charitable isolation of the disputed variable, while recognizing that a methodological challenge is not itself positive evidence.

con-historical-plausibility-of-miracle-r.words: Historians compare unprecedented miracle reports with historically familiar invention or alteration and may find the latter more probable without declaring the reported miracle impossible.
con-historical-plausibility-of-miracle-r.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly answers the matched-story challenge by distinguishing metaphysical possibility from historical establishment and requiring comparison between a miracle report and familiar mechanisms such as alteration, mistake, or invention. Principal limitation: Its suggestion that an unprecedented miracle cannot be historically established is stronger than the general comparative argument supplied, because sufficiently powerful evidence could conceptually overcome a low prior without abandoning ordinary historical reasoning. Live burden: The skeptical case must evaluate the actual strength, independence, and provenance of the resurrection reports instead of allowing unprecedented content to function as a fixed evidentiary ceiling. Locked score: The very strong band reflects high responsiveness, central relevance, explicit qualification, and a coherent probabilistic framework, moderated because its categorical-sounding methodological boundary slightly outruns the warrant developed in this exchange.

pro-attestation-can-raise-miracle-probab.words: Numerous independent reports, especially from witnesses disposed toward skepticism, should be capable of increasing the historical probability assigned to an apparent miracle.
pro-attestation-can-raise-miracle-probab.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies multiplicity, independence, and skeptical disposition as concrete evidentiary properties that could raise the probability of an extraordinary event, effectively denying that rarity makes testimony historically inert. Principal limitation: The claim remains hypothetical and leaves its threshold undefined, while supplying no demonstration that the surviving resurrection materials actually constitute numerous independent reports from initially skeptical witnesses. Live burden: The pro case must connect this sound probabilistic possibility to the documentary record, distinguish genuinely independent attestation from literary dependence, and show that the resulting increase exceeds ordinary-error explanations rather than merely moving probability upward. Locked score: The very strong band reflects coherent calibration, direct methodological relevance, and fair acknowledgment of low prior frequency, tempered by modest evidence warrant because the decisive application to the resurrection accounts remains undeveloped.

con-probabilistic-historical-establishme.words: Historians should compare proposed miracles with familiar alternatives and report only what surviving evidence establishes as probable, without categorically denying extraordinary events.
con-probabilistic-historical-establishme.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies the requested noncategorical standard, distinguishing what happened in the inaccessible past from what surviving evidence probably establishes and explicitly comparing testimony with witness error, dependence, or fabrication. Principal limitation: Although methodologically clear, the move states the comparison more fully than it performs it, offering no detailed likelihood analysis of the actual resurrection witnesses, sources, and alternative mechanisms within this excerpt. Live burden: The skeptical route must apply its comparative framework consistently, allowing strong attestation to raise probability while showing why the concrete ordinary alternatives remain superior on the available record. Locked score: The very strong band reflects outstanding responsiveness to both methodological challenges, precise qualification, central relevance, logical coherence, and charitable treatment of extraordinary possibilities, with limited restraint for its relatively general evidentiary application.

pro-acts-ending-supports-early-date.words: Acts ends with Paul alive in Rome and omits subsequent upheavals, supporting an early-sixties composition that would place Luke-Acts nearer its narrated events.
pro-acts-ending-supports-early-date.critique: Strongest feature: The argument identifies conspicuous omitted events, including later persecution, war, and the temple’s destruction, then offers a clear chronological inference from Acts ending while Paul remains alive in Rome. Principal limitation: It treats authorial ignorance as the most straightforward explanation without comparatively testing thematic closure, selective scope, or literary purpose, so the omission supports but does not secure an early date. Live burden: The pro case must show that a narrative ending is more expected under early composition than under later literary design and explain how the proposed date addresses anonymity, dependence, contradiction, and transmission separately. Locked score: The strong band reflects substantial central relevance, a concrete textual datum, and direct contact with the dating component of the skeptical case, moderated by overstated calibration and incomplete coverage of that broader source-critical argument.

con-concrete-gospel-contradictions.words: Concrete Gospel contradictions demonstrate authorial alteration of inherited material and prevent every account from being simultaneously inerrant, without rendering all Gospel history worthless.
con-concrete-gospel-contradictions.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers concrete incompatible details, distinguishes smaller discrepancies from consequential chronology, and draws the narrow necessary conclusion that mutually exclusive accounts cannot all be simultaneously inerrant. Principal limitation: Establishing alteration and defeating inerrancy does not by itself quantify how much historically usable material remains, determine which author is preferable, or show that the central resurrection claims share the same defect. Live burden: The skeptical case must translate specific contradictions into appropriately bounded conclusions about independence, accuracy, and resurrection testimony while preserving the admitted possibility of broadly reliable content. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent logical entailment, strong textual warrant, maximal central relevance, explicit scope control, and unusually charitable separation of historical interpretation from inerrancy, with only modest unresolved work concerning the wider consequences of contradiction.

pro-variation-compatible-with-testimony.words: Errors, compression, and divergent interpretation can occur in sincere eyewitness-derived mediation, so Gospel discrepancies defeat strict inerrancy without making the accounts historically worthless.
pro-variation-compatible-with-testimony.critique: Strongest feature: The reply carefully separates inerrancy from historical usefulness and claims compatibility rather than proof, granting ordinary error while directly resisting the inference from discrepancy to worthless or wholly detached testimony. Principal limitation: Its memoir analogy is anecdotal and does not establish that the actual Gospel contradictions arose under comparable conditions, from independent memories, or within transmission capable of preserving the central events accurately. Live burden: The pro route must examine the concrete variations, distinguish ordinary testimonial divergence from theological alteration, and supply positive evidence that witness-derived continuity explains the documents better than layered literary development. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise calibration, major direct responsiveness, central relevance, and charitable concession of error, tempered because general compatibility with sincere testimony cannot verify the provenance or reliability of these particular accounts.

pro-local-knowledge-supports-continuity.words: Accurate Palestinian geography and period-appropriate names indicate retained local knowledge across transmission, giving the Gospels historical credit despite chronological and linguistic distance.
pro-local-knowledge-supports-continuity.critique: Strongest feature: The move presses a concrete asymmetry in the transmission hypothesis, asking why decades and geographical distance did not produce widespread errors in Palestinian names and geography if connection with the setting had substantially dissolved. Principal limitation: Accurate local details can be preserved, researched, or inherited independently of particular sayings and episodes, so the argument slides from cultural continuity toward broader historical credit without a sufficiently domain-specific bridge. Live burden: The pro case must show that the mechanisms preserving geography and naming patterns also make accurate event testimony likely, while addressing anonymity, literary dependence, and selective theological change. Locked score: The strong band reflects pertinent continuity evidence, direct pressure on an expected-error implication, and substantial central relevance, moderated by partly unstable scope, implicit qualification, and incomplete engagement with selective preservation.

con-visions-originated-resurrection-beli.words: Some followers likely experienced post-crucifixion visions, came to believe Jesus was alive, and persuaded others, although the evidence does not establish bodily resurrection.
con-visions-originated-resurrection-beli.critique: Strongest feature: The reconstruction is explicitly calibrated about the unknown number and grouping of experiences, separates followers’ conviction from historical establishment, and supplies a familiar initial mechanism for the rise of resurrection belief. Principal limitation: Visions explain the first convictions more readily than the complete doctrinal content, bodily emphasis, persistent doubt, collective spread, and durable missionary consequences, leaving several important causal links compressed. Live burden: The skeptical case must develop a multistage account showing how limited experiences, persuasion, prior commitments, and social transmission generated the movement’s distinctive claims without assuming that every follower shared an identical vision. Locked score: The very strong band reflects coherent central-burden contact, candid uncertainty, proportionate force, and a plausible ordinary starting point, moderated by incomplete explanatory coverage and limited direct testing of the bodily-resurrection alternative.

con-empty-tomb-narrative-not-verificatio.words: The empty-tomb passages possess emotional power, but their narrated production of doubt rather than faith does not independently verify either the tomb or resurrection historically.
con-empty-tomb-narrative-not-verificatio.critique: Strongest feature: The move sharply separates literary or emotional power from historical occurrence and observes that, within the narratives, the empty tomb generates doubt rather than functioning as self-sufficient verification of resurrection. Principal limitation: It does not answer the selected local-knowledge argument, and its narrative observation cannot itself establish that the empty-tomb tradition was invented or lacked evidentiary significance when combined with appearances. Live burden: The skeptical case must connect the literary function of doubt to source history and explain why psychological realism or cumulative evidence does not support an underlying event, rather than relying on nonverification alone. Locked score: The strong band reflects clear scope, coherent qualification, useful subsidiary relevance, and charitable acknowledgment of the passages’ force, reduced by its nonanswer to the decisive earlier target and limited independent warrant about historicity.

pro-doubt-psychologically-realistic.words: Doubt is a natural reaction to an unprecedented bodily return, so Doubting Thomas and requests for touch are compatible with psychologically realistic narration.
pro-doubt-psychologically-realistic.critique: Strongest feature: The concise reply uses the agreed rarity of resurrection to explain why doubt and a request for physical contact would be psychologically natural rather than narratively embarrassing or intrinsically suspicious. Principal limitation: Psychological compatibility is not positive evidence of occurrence, and the move does not answer the opponent’s separate claim that neither narrated doubt nor an empty tomb independently verifies resurrection historically. Live burden: The pro case must show that these details are more expected as preserved experiential memory than as literary characterization or apologetic construction, using criteria beyond intuitive realism alone. Locked score: The strong band reflects lucid reasoning, proportionate plausibility, a fitting textual example, and direct contact with one interpretive component, moderated by subsidiary relevance, limited comparative evidence, and incomplete responsiveness to the decisive verification distinction.

pro-bereavement-visions-explanatorily-in.words: Common bereavement visions inadequately explain the early combination of radical bodily claims, continuing doubt, missionary activity, and the sudden formation of a new religion.
pro-bereavement-visions-explanatorily-in.critique: Strongest feature: The objection identifies multiple explananda beyond an initial experience, including radical bodily claims, persistent doubt, missionary action, and movement formation, thereby exposing the limits of a simple bereavement-vision analogy. Principal limitation: It moves from dissimilarity toward explanatory insufficiency without comparing stronger natural models involving a few visionaries, prior messianic commitment, persuasion, social amplification, and later theological development. Live burden: The pro route must specify a rival causal account and establish the earliest form and interdependence of its listed phenomena, rather than treating the religion’s eventual scale as direct evidence for resurrection. Locked score: The strong band reflects important central-burden contact, substantial responsiveness, and a concrete explanatory challenge, moderated by implicit qualifications, partly unstable causal scope, limited documentation, and incomplete engagement with a multistage alternative.

con-messianic-reinterpretation-after-vis.words: Followers already committed to Jesus as Messiah interpreted visions after his death as vindication, recasting the crucifixion as divinely intended, salvific, and followed by resurrection.
con-messianic-reinterpretation-after-vis.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies a coherent multistage mechanism connecting disappointed messianic expectations, reported visions, acknowledgment of prior misunderstanding, divine vindication, salvific reinterpretation, and the emergence of resurrection belief. Principal limitation: It implicitly generalizes from some visionaries to a broader group and does not fully explain continuing doubt, missionary scale, bodily narrative detail, or why this particular reinterpretation prevailed over abandonment. Live burden: The skeptical route must provide evidence for each causal transition and integrate social diffusion with its literary-development account, while allowing that original experiences may have been interpreted differently by different followers. Locked score: The strong band reflects high logical coherence, direct central relevance, a substantial answer to the insufficiency objection, and fair recognition of the opposing demand, moderated by incomplete responsiveness and limited evidence for collective generalization.

con-bodily-scenes-as-polemical-developme.words: Luke’s and John’s fish-eating and wound-touching scenes plausibly answer Christians favoring spiritual resurrection and express Jewish expectations of a genuinely bodily resurrection.
con-bodily-scenes-as-polemical-developme.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers a concrete rival explanation for fish eating and wound touching by connecting those scenes to disputes over spiritual versus physical resurrection and to a recognizably bodily theological purpose. Principal limitation: A later polemical use does not establish invention, because inherited experiential traditions could also serve apologetic aims, and the asserted direction and intention require fuller evidence concerning dating and literary dependence. Live burden: The skeptical case must distinguish adaptation from creation, demonstrate that the disputed context predicts these scenes better than preserved memory does, and explain the remaining doubt and misrecognition material. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct responsiveness to the authenticity inference, coherent subsidiary relevance, identifiable historical context, and a serious alternative function, tempered by slightly overstated calibration and incomplete accommodation of traditions that are both inherited and polemically deployed.

pro-narrative-strangeness-as-experientia.words: Empty-tomb traditions, doubt, misrecognition, physical contact, eating, and supernatural movement form an awkward mixture that suggests experiential strangeness rather than simple later advocacy.
pro-narrative-strangeness-as-experientia.critique: Strongest feature: The move gathers several resistant features into a direct challenge to a single-purpose advocacy model, emphasizing how doubt, misrecognition, physicality, eating, and supernatural movement produce a narratively awkward rather than smoothly triumphant account. Principal limitation: Literary complexity is compatible with layered sources, inherited traditions, and multiple apologetic aims, so awkwardness alone underdetermines whether the material traces an original bodily encounter or later development. Live burden: The pro case must articulate criteria by which experiential residue can be distinguished from compositional layering and show why the entire cluster is more probable under witness-derived memory. Locked score: The strong band reflects wide responsiveness, concrete textual attention, and meaningful pressure on an overly simple polemical account, moderated by unstable terminology, limited comparative warrant, and underdeveloped charity toward the strongest layered-development alternative.

strengths: Douthat isolated the methodological effect of miraculous content through a controlled comparison instead of merely accusing historical skepticism of prejudice.
He correctly distinguished fallible, mediated testimony from inerrancy and showed that contradiction does not logically entail total historical worthlessness.
His local-knowledge and Acts arguments supplied concrete documentary considerations supporting continuity and earlier proximity rather than relying only on general trust.
He pressed the visionary account to explain bodily claims, persistent doubt, missionary activity, and movement formation as a connected causal package.
His closing appeal to narrative strangeness directly engaged the literary-development explanation across several awkward resurrection details.

blunders.text: The hypothetical attestation threshold was never connected rigorously to the actual number, independence, provenance, or skeptical disposition of the resurrection sources.
Accurate names and geography were asked to carry broader historical credit without establishing that sayings and narrated events were preserved by the same mechanisms.
The argument from Acts’ ending insufficiently compared early composition with thematic or literary reasons for ending while Paul preached in Rome.
Narrative oddity and psychological realism remained compatible with layered literary development, so neither became strong positive evidence for occurrence.

strengths: Ehrman combined dependence, anonymity, dating, linguistic distance, oral transmission, and contradiction while still allowing that the Gospels preserve credible history.
He used concrete incompatible Gospel details to defeat simultaneous inerrancy without inflating that conclusion into wholesale historical skepticism.
His probabilistic account of historical establishment directly answered both the miracle-content challenge and the proposed power of abundant attestation.
He calibrated the visionary reconstruction carefully, acknowledging uncertainty about the number and grouping of experiences rather than asserting uniform hallucination.
He supplemented visions with messianic reinterpretation and polemical literary development, producing a more complete ordinary causal explanation.

blunders.text: The initial source-transmission case compressed the inference from conditions permitting change to evidence that the particular resurrection traditions materially changed.
The claim that unprecedented miracles cannot be historically established sounded stronger than the comparative probabilistic method itself warranted.
The empty-tomb response did not contact the earlier local-knowledge argument selected as its decisive target and therefore functioned as relevant contrary material rather than an answer.
The natural reconstruction still left persistent doubt, collective diffusion, missionary scale, and the precise development of bodily content only partly explained.

newArguments.title: Discriminating-evidence test
newArguments.text: Instead of counting reports, compare what each hypothesis predicts. A bodily encounter may predict durable conviction alongside shock, doubt, tactile checking, and difficulty describing continuity and transformation. A vision-plus-development model may predict visionary conviction and later bodily elaboration. The pro case improves only if the earliest recoverable evidence contains the first cluster before the proposed polemical pressures could readily generate it. This test converts narrative strangeness from an intuition into a comparative research program and permits the skeptical hypothesis to prevail when the chronology runs the other way.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a hypothesis-prediction framework not stated in any locked participant move.

newArguments.title: Correlated-cost caution
newArguments.text: The skeptical explanation invokes several ordinary mechanisms: visions, persuasion, reinterpretation, oral change, literary dependence, and polemical development. Those mechanisms cannot simply be multiplied as independent advantages, because some may be correlated or require specific sequencing. A cumulative pro case can ask whether the full natural reconstruction becomes less economical once timing, social transmission, bodily interpretation, and resistant details are jointly constrained. This does not prove resurrection; it identifies a fair comparative burden that evaluates complete causal packages rather than contrasting one extraordinary claim with an unpriced collection of ordinary possibilities.

novelty.explanation: This adds a causal-model complexity argument while expressly limiting its historical conclusion.

newArguments.title: Chronological layering test
newArguments.text: The skeptical case can be made testable by ordering the evidence rather than merely labeling scenes late. First identify the earliest recoverable claims; then track when empty-tomb detail, tactile verification, eating, misrecognition, and supernatural movement become textually visible. If increasingly concrete bodily demonstrations appear alongside identifiable controversies over spiritual resurrection, development gains explanatory support. If the complete awkward cluster is independently early, that support weakens. This chronological test answers the objection that polemical usefulness does not prove invention and prevents source criticism from becoming a generic explanation applied regardless of sequence.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit chronological prediction capable of supporting or weakening literary development.

newArguments.title: Network-diffusion model
newArguments.text: A new movement does not require many identical founding experiences. A small number of high-trust visionaries can influence close associates; shared messianic expectations provide interpretive vocabulary; communal rehearsal stabilizes selected claims; missionary success then rewards portable formulations. This network model predicts sincere conviction, uneven doubt, and rapid spread without treating participants as deceptive or psychologically uniform. Its force depends on evidence for authority relationships and communication pathways, but it directly addresses the claim that ordinary bereavement experiences cannot plausibly set a durable religion in motion.

novelty.explanation: This adds a social-network mechanism absent from the locked visionary and reinterpretation moves.
